verdict.rationale: Sentry's own Alerts docs say an alert rule can 'call webhooks' when issues match pre-defined rules, so outbound HTTP callbacks exist as a product feature. The evidence shows them only as an alert action, not as a general event-subscription system. Slack, PagerDuty and Twilio notifications and Splunk data forwarding do not count toward this story. Missing for 10: a documented webhook registration flow or API, a catalog of subscribable event types beyond alert-rule matches, payload schema, signature verification and retry semantics, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: An alert can send notifications, create tickets, call webhooks, or use other integrations
An alert can send notifications, create tickets, call webhooks, or use other integrations for issues coming from projects or Monitors.
Sentry's **Alerts** take action when issues in your organization match pre-defined rules.
